more_info.overview: Alkaline-treated starch is food starch modified by treatment with sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide. JECFA describes this treatment as causing limited fragmentation of the original starch structure. The preparation has thickening, stabilising, binding or emulsifying functions. Non-pregelatinised material retains starch granules and is insoluble in cold water but develops a viscous dispersion in hot water. The modification is distinct from acetylation or phosphate crosslinking.
more_info.origin: Plant starch chemically treated with sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide. The specification does not restrict this identity to one botanical starch source.
